definitions.inequality: A comparison of expressions using <, >, ≤, or ≥ instead of equality.
definitions.solution set: All values satisfying an inequality or set of conditions.
definitions.boundary: A value separating included and excluded regions of a number-line solution.
definitions.open endpoint: A boundary value not included in the solution, shown with an open circle.
definitions.closed endpoint: A boundary value included in the solution, shown with a filled circle.
definitions.interval notation: A way of writing intervals using brackets for included endpoints and parentheses for excluded endpoints.
definitions.compound inequality: A statement joining two inequalities, often using AND or OR.
definitions.intersection: Values common to every named solution set, used for an AND condition.
definitions.union: Values belonging to at least one named solution set, used for an OR condition.
definitions.AND: The logical requirement that both stated conditions must hold.
definitions.OR: The logical requirement that at least one stated condition must hold.
definitions.absolute value: The nonnegative distance of a real number from zero, written |x|.
definitions.distance: The nonnegative length between two points, such as |a-b| on a number line.
definitions.tolerance: An allowed amount of variation from a target value.
definitions.feasible set: The values satisfying all the constraints in a mathematical model.
definitions.constraint: A requirement or limit an acceptable value or solution must satisfy.
definitions.sign reversal: When multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, reverse its comparison symbol.
